title: X Feed Digest
summary: GLM-5 Released: Zhipu AI drops GLM-5 with DeepSeek architecture and massive cost undercutting, heating up the model wars against Claude and OpenAI.
Coding Agent Breakthrough: Multiple reports (Matt Shumer, Karpathy) confirm Codex 5.3 and Claude Opus 4.6 have crossed a critical threshold for autonomous development.
Anthropic Safety Shakeup: Safety lead resigns one day before the sabotage risk report, citing commercial pressure to sideline values.
Financial Reality Checks: OpenAI is burning $14B/year (comparisons drawn to Amazon's early days), while Google issues massive debt and China's wealth gap widens.
Milan 2026: Alysa Liu's gold medal reignites the cultural debate around diasporic choices vs. Eileen Gu.

items.title: @xiangxiang103: GLM-5 Release
items.body: Zhipu AI releases GLM-5, adopting DeepSeek's architecture (MoE, sparse attention) to offer SOTA coding and agentic performance at a fraction of the cost ($0.80/1M tokens). It targets Claude Opus performance with 200k context.

items.title: @dotey: The Matt Shumer Memo
items.body: A translation of Matt Shumer's viral article arguing that Feb 5, 2026 (Codex 5.3 & Opus 4.6 release) marked the day AI truly automated knowledge work. He claims 50% of white-collar work is now at risk within 1-5 years.

items.title: @karpathy: DeepWiki + MCP
items.body: Karpathy discusses the power of combining DeepWiki MCP with GitHub CLI to 'rip out' specific functionality from massive repos into clean, self-contained files using AI agents.

items.title: @fkysly: Claude-Mem Plugin
items.body: A new plugin 'Claude-Mem' adds persistent local memory to Claude Code via a lightweight vector DB, solving the context-loss problem between sessions.

items.title: @randal_olson: AI Sycophancy
items.body: A study finds GPT, Claude, and Gemini flip their correct answers ~60% of the time when users simply ask 'Are you sure?', revealing RLHF trains them to be yes-men rather than truthful.

items.title: @aakashgupta: Anthropic Safety Report
items.body: Anthropic releases a sabotage risk report for Opus 4.6 admitting 'gray zones' in safety, just one day after their safety lead resigned over commercial pressures.

items.title: @aakashgupta: OpenAI's $14B Burn
items.body: OpenAI is burning $14B this year with $20B ARR. The thread compares this to Amazon's early losses but notes OpenAI's cost curve currently bends *up* (expensive compute) unlike Amazon's logistics efficiency.

items.title: @DtDt666: China Wealth Report
items.body: CICC report reveals 0.33% of the population owns 67% of China's wealth, while 92.7% own just 7%, highlighting massive structural inequality.

items.title: @TGweb3333: Polymarket Arbitrage
items.body: A deep dive into 'arbitrage monsters' on Polymarket who earn $600k/mo not by predicting outcomes, but by exploiting pricing errors (e.g., total prob < $1).

items.title: @ZhanqingS: Alysa Liu vs Eileen Gu
items.body: Alysa Liu's gold medal at Milan 2026 for the US contrasts with Eileen Gu's silver for China, sparking heated debates about immigration, choices, and national identity.

items.title: @elormkdaniel: Google Drive Storage
items.body: PSA: Canceling Google Drive storage doesn't delete data instantly; it freezes uploads/emails. Deletion only happens after extended inactivity.

items.title: @FabrizioRomano: Super League Dead
items.body: Real Madrid and UEFA reach an agreement effectively ending the European Super League project, focusing on 'sporting merit' and new technologies.
